title: TrackGNN: A Highly Parallelized and Self-Adaptive GNN Accelerator for Track Reconstruction on FPGAs
problem: Real-time track reconstruction in high energy physics experiments requires processing graph neural networks under strict latency constraints that prevent deployment on general-purpose CPU and GPU platforms.
motivation: Efficient hardware acceleration of graph neural networks is essential for real-time track reconstruction in high energy physics experiments to meet stringent latency requirements.
method: TrackGNN employs a dataflow architecture with multiple levels of parallelism to accelerate GNN computations on FPGAs. A self-adaptive renaming mechanism optimizes the processing of graph structures to reduce latency. The design combines data parallelism and adaptive scheduling to improve both performance and resource efficiency.
key_novelty: Self-adaptive renaming mechanism that reduces end-to-end latency with negligible resource overhead compared to prior FPGA GNN accelerators like FlowGNN.
contributions: Dataflow-based FPGA GNN accelerator architecture with multiple parallelism levels
Self-adaptive renaming mechanism for optimizing latency in graph processing
Open-source implementation achieving 27.6× speedup over CPU and up to 101.1× over GPU
1.12-1.16× latency reduction versus FlowGNN with minimal resource overhead

metrics.speedup: 27.6× over CPU, 101.1× over GPU, 5.7× over FPGA overlay

limitations: Limitations not explicitly discussed in abstract; evaluation focuses on performance speedups and latency comparisons.
